item.title: Re: Mommy, Daddy, look! A rainbow!
item.content:encoded:
Hello jacked-anime-cole! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: Eight human-looking entities created when shining a specific spotlight at a special prism.

While the premise sounds doable, there isn't enough specific information here to really get an idea of what the skip is. The concept doesn't really show what the skips motives or purpose is, or expand upon the base idea. Overall there isn't much to get invested in here as the concept is too vague.

-Some general things to expand on:

-What are these entities
-why are they important
-what is their purpose
-what part does the prism play in all of this
-why should I as the reader care about the concept? what will make me invested?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: There is none yet, but will be very soon! :)

I would highly recommend developing some sort of narrative before posting, as they help give a direction to the concept and can help with audience engagement. Articles featuring a narrative tend to favoured by modern audiences, which has more or less lead to Articles with a narrative becoming the standard. -the narrative doesn't need to be super detailed and long, short stories also work very well (it mostly comes down to execution).

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A corrosive light from a spotlight and a hazardous prism come together to shine eight colours on a wall, from Red all the way to Pink.

This feels closer to a brief summary of the skip, as there isn't much other than the skips characteristics and functions shown here. What about this will make me invested? what are the implications of this? how should this make the reader feel?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

Notes:

Additional Notes: I need help with the attention grabber and the central narrative. If anyone has ideas PLEASE tell me them! Thank you!

Generally speaking, I would recommend expanding upon what you currently have. Try to get an idea on what the skips end goal is (or purpose is), and use that to get an idea on the overall narrative and central conflict.- don't be afraid to experiment with different endings or motives!

- Try to get an idea on where the narrative will start and end, that way the middle act and conflict will be easier to put together.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED
